quests.hint: The word that shows moving from standing to sitting.
quests.explanation: 'Sit down' means move into a seated position. Phrasal verbs combine a verb and a particle, and the particle changes the meaning: 'sit', 'sit down', 'sit up'.
quests.textToSpeak: You look tired. Why don't you sit ___ and I'll make you a cup of tea?
quests.correctAnswer: You look tired. Why don't you sit down and I'll make you a cup of tea?
quests.contextClue: A tired person who is offered tea will need somewhere to rest.

quests.hint: A past-tense verb; with 'off' it means the plane left the ground.
quests.explanation: 'Take off' is used for planes leaving the ground. It is irregular: take, took, taken. As a noun it is written 'takeoff'.
quests.textToSpeak: The plane was delayed, but it finally ___ off an hour late.
quests.correctAnswer: The plane was delayed, but it finally took off an hour late.
quests.contextClue: A flight that left late after a delay.

quests.hint: With 'out of', this verb means you have none left.
quests.explanation: 'Run out of' + noun means use all of something: 'run out of milk'. The thing that is finished comes after 'of'.
quests.textToSpeak: We've ___ out of coffee. I'll buy some on the way home.
quests.correctAnswer: We've run out of coffee. I'll buy some on the way home.
quests.contextClue: Needing to buy more shows the supply is finished.

quests.hint: Discover a piece of information.
quests.explanation: 'Find out' means get information about something. Use 'find' alone for an object you were searching for: 'I found my wallet'.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll ___ out what time the shop opens and text you.
quests.correctAnswer: I'll find out what time the shop opens and text you.
quests.contextClue: Promising a text afterwards means the speaker will first get the answer.

quests.hint: Continue; with 'on', it means keep going.
quests.explanation: 'Carry on' means continue. It is often followed by 'with' + noun or by -ing: 'carry on with your work', 'carry on talking'.
quests.textToSpeak: Sorry to interrupt. Please ___ on with what you were saying.
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry to interrupt. Please carry on with what you were saying.
quests.contextClue: An interruption is followed by an invitation to continue.

quests.hint: The -ing form of a verb that, with 'off', means delaying.
quests.explanation: 'Put off' + -ing means delay doing something: 'put off cleaning'. The verb after it takes -ing.
quests.textToSpeak: I keep ___ off cleaning the garage because it's such a big job.
quests.correctAnswer: I keep putting off cleaning the garage because it's such a big job.
quests.contextClue: A big job explains why it keeps being delayed.

quests.hint: Collect someone from a place.
quests.explanation: 'Pick up' someone means collect them, often by car. The pronoun goes in the middle: 'pick them up'.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you ___ up the kids from school today? I'm stuck at work.
quests.correctAnswer: Could you pick up the kids from school today? I'm stuck at work.
quests.contextClue: Being stuck at work explains why a favour is needed.

quests.hint: The past tense of a verb meaning stopped working.
quests.explanation: 'Break down' is used for vehicles and machines that stop working. It is irregular: break, broke, broken.
quests.textToSpeak: The car ___ down on the motorway, so we waited for a tow truck.
quests.correctAnswer: The car broke down on the motorway, so we waited for a tow truck.
quests.contextClue: A tow truck implies the car couldn't be driven.

quests.hint: The past tense of the verb for spending your childhood somewhere.
quests.explanation: 'Grow up' means spend your childhood and become an adult. It is irregular: grow, grew, grown. A place follows with 'in'.
quests.textToSpeak: They were born in Lagos, but they ___ up in Toronto.
quests.correctAnswer: They were born in Lagos, but they grew up in Toronto.
quests.contextClue: 'Born in... but' contrasts the birthplace with the childhood place.

quests.hint: Stop trying.
quests.explanation: 'Give up' means stop trying. It can take a noun ('give up smoking') or stand alone ('Don't give up').
quests.textToSpeak: Don't ___ up! Everyone fails sometimes, and you can try again.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't give up! Everyone fails sometimes, and you can try again.
quests.contextClue: The encouragement to try again shows the listener is close to quitting.

quests.hint: Register to join something.
quests.explanation: 'Sign up (for)' means register to join something. The noun is 'sign-up'.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd like to ___ up for your newsletter; where do I enter my email?
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to sign up for your newsletter; where do I enter my email?
quests.contextClue: Entering an email suggests registering.

quests.hint: Exercise to stay fit.
quests.explanation: 'Work out' has several meanings: exercise, solve, or calculate. Here it means exercise. The noun is 'workout'.
quests.textToSpeak: I try to ___ out three times a week, mostly by running and swimming.
quests.correctAnswer: I try to work out three times a week, mostly by running and swimming.
quests.contextClue: Running and swimming are the kind of activity being described.

quests.hint: Confuse one thing with another.
quests.explanation: 'Mix up' means confuse one with another. It is separable: 'mix the names up'. The noun is 'mix-up'.
quests.textToSpeak: I always ___ up the twins' names; they look so alike.
quests.correctAnswer: I always mix up the twins' names; they look so alike.
quests.contextClue: Similar looks explain the confusion.

quests.hint: Leave a course before finishing it.
quests.explanation: 'Drop out (of)' means leave school or a course before finishing. The noun is 'dropout'.
quests.textToSpeak: He decided to ___ out of university after the first year.
quests.correctAnswer: He decided to drop out of university after the first year.
quests.contextClue: Deciding after the first year means not finishing.

quests.hint: Think of an idea.
quests.explanation: 'Come up with' + idea means think of or produce it: 'come up with a plan'. A noun follows.
quests.textToSpeak: We need to ___ up with a better name for the product.
quests.correctAnswer: We need to come up with a better name for the product.
quests.contextClue: A better name has to be created.

quests.hint: The word that means gone from this place.
quests.explanation: With smells, pain or stains, 'go away' means disappear. Also: 'the pain went away'.
quests.textToSpeak: The smell of paint won't go ___, even with the windows open.
quests.correctAnswer: The smell of paint won't go away, even with the windows open.
quests.contextClue: Open windows haven't removed the smell.

quests.hint: The word that follows 'called' to mean cancelled.
quests.explanation: 'Call off' means cancel something planned. Here it appears in the passive: 'was called off'.
quests.textToSpeak: The concert was called ___ because of the storm.
quests.correctAnswer: The concert was called off because of the storm.
quests.contextClue: A storm is the reason the event did not happen.

quests.hint: The opposite of going out.
quests.explanation: 'Stay in' means remain at home rather than go out. 'Stay out' means the opposite.
quests.textToSpeak: I can't go out tonight. I have to stay ___ and finish my presentation.
quests.correctAnswer: I can't go out tonight. I have to stay in and finish my presentation.
quests.contextClue: Work prevents the speaker from going anywhere.

quests.hint: Reduce; the verb can also mean using a knife.
quests.explanation: 'Cut down on' + noun means reduce how much you use or eat: 'cut down on coffee'. 'Cut back on' is similar.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm trying to ___ down on sugar in my tea.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm trying to cut down on sugar in my tea.
quests.contextClue: Reducing sugar in tea is a change in habit.

quests.hint: Finish in an unexpected situation.
quests.explanation: 'End up' + -ing describes an unplanned result: 'end up waiting'. It can also take a place: 'end up in Paris'.
quests.textToSpeak: If you don't check the timetable, you'll ___ up waiting an hour for the next train.
quests.correctAnswer: If you don't check the timetable, you'll end up waiting an hour for the next train.
quests.contextClue: Not checking leads to an unwelcome outcome.

quests.hint: Disappoint people who depend on you.
quests.explanation: 'Let down' means disappoint: 'don't let me down'. It is separable: 'let the team down'.
quests.textToSpeak: Please be on time; I don't want to ___ the team down.
quests.correctAnswer: Please be on time; I don't want to let the team down.
quests.contextClue: The team depends on punctuality.

quests.hint: Handle a situation or person.
quests.explanation: 'Deal with' means handle or manage: 'deal with a problem'. It is always followed by 'with'.
quests.textToSpeak: Leave it to me. I'll ___ with the supplier myself.
quests.correctAnswer: Leave it to me. I'll deal with the supplier myself.
quests.contextClue: The speaker takes responsibility for a task.

quests.hint: Mention a topic.
quests.explanation: 'Bring up' means mention a subject. It can also mean raise a child. It is separable: 'bring it up'.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't ___ up the argument at dinner; everyone is still upset.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't bring up the argument at dinner; everyone is still upset.
quests.contextClue: A sensitive topic should not be raised.

quests.hint: The -ing form of a verb meaning to draw attention to something.
quests.explanation: 'Point out' means draw attention to something. After 'thanks for', use the -ing form.
quests.textToSpeak: Thanks for ___ out the typo before I sent the invitation.
quests.correctAnswer: Thanks for pointing out the typo before I sent the invitation.
quests.contextClue: The error was noticed and mentioned before sending.

quests.hint: It follows 'get' when a phone call connects.
quests.explanation: 'Get through' (to someone) means succeed in reaching them by phone. It also has other meanings, such as surviving a difficult time.
quests.textToSpeak: I couldn't get ___ to the helpline; the line was busy all morning.
quests.correctAnswer: I couldn't get through to the helpline; the line was busy all morning.
quests.contextClue: A busy line stopped the call from connecting.

quests.hint: In separate pieces.
quests.explanation: 'Fall apart' means break into pieces or fail completely. It works for objects, plans and relationships.
quests.textToSpeak: The old book was so worn that it fell ___ in my hands.
quests.correctAnswer: The old book was so worn that it fell apart in my hands.
quests.contextClue: A worn book breaking up when handled.

quests.hint: The word that links 'go' and 'with' when you accept a group decision.
quests.explanation: 'Go along with' means accept or follow a decision, often without full enthusiasm. Pattern: go along with + noun.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not sure about the plan, but I'll go ___ with it because everyone else agrees.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm not sure about the plan, but I'll go along with it because everyone else agrees.
quests.contextClue: Doubt is followed by agreement with the group.

quests.hint: Recover from.
quests.explanation: 'Get over' + illness or a bad experience means recover from it. It can also mean cross something.
quests.textToSpeak: It took me weeks to get ___ the flu.
quests.correctAnswer: It took me weeks to get over the flu.
quests.contextClue: Weeks of illness suggest a slow recovery.

quests.hint: The word after 'look' that makes it mean 'investigate'.
quests.explanation: 'Look into' means investigate. It differs from 'look at', which only means direct your eyes toward something.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager promised to look ___ the missing payment and find out what went wrong.
quests.correctAnswer: The manager promised to look into the missing payment and find out what went wrong.
quests.contextClue: Finding out what went wrong is an investigation.

quests.hint: The word that adds urgency after 'hurry'.
quests.explanation: 'Hurry up' urges someone to go faster. In fast speech you will also hear 'Come on!' or 'Let's go!'
quests.textToSpeak: Come on, hurry ___! The bus leaves in two minutes.
quests.correctAnswer: Come on, hurry up! The bus leaves in two minutes.
quests.contextClue: Two minutes is the time pressure.
